operations.coverage: typed column-to-parameter and same-type column-to-column comparisons for supported comparison operators, single-value IN/NOT IN, separate typed lower/upper BETWEEN bounds, LIKE/ILIKE patterns, and IS NULL/IS NOT NULL with nested AND/OR/NOT; groups are bounded to depth 32 and 128 nodes
typed aggregate comparisons with nested AND, OR, and NOT

typed identifier, literal, binary operator, arithmetic unary sign, CAST/TRY_CAST/SAFE_CAST/::/CONVERT/TRY_CONVERT target type and CAST wrapper, registered aggregate wrapper, searched CASE wrapper, typed IN/NOT IN/BETWEEN/NOT BETWEEN/LIKE/NOT LIKE/IS NULL/IS NOT NULL predicate templates, editable IN-list value append/remove, WHERE clause seed, CTE rename/add-seed/remove-unreferenced, set-operation operator/quantifier/add-seed/remove-one-operand/swap-operands, supported predicate negation, CASE branch/ELSE, typed projection expression replacement, binary expression construction on a selected SELECT item or expression node from same-query typed operands, same-query expression replacement, projection append/removal/reorder, GROUP BY expression append, and ORDER BY expression append; reorder is limited to comment-free SELECT lists and removal rejects comments in the removed span; aggregate argument edits follow the Rust registry, and scalar subquery projection seed
non-negative integer literals; both clauses can be added, edited, or removed

limits: one relation selected from trusted Form context
relation-free SELECT 1 draft can select a Form
plain aliases on a single relation are supported and preserved; edited column references remain unqualified
self-join relations are resolved from the same trusted Form context
relation-free integer/string/boolean/NULL literal projections
typed literal projection edits are restricted to those relation-free literals
wildcard or simple columns
a selected SELECT item or expression node can be composed from two typed expression nodes in the same query scope with a closed binary operator
a selected supported expression node can be wrapped in a typed CAST target through a Rust-rendered operation; comment-bearing, other-expression, and subquery spans fail closed
a selected typed projection expression can be wrapped in COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, or MAX, with the single-argument DISTINCT option taken from the shared aggregate registry
simple Form-column projection aliases are inspected and edited independently by SQL-document-scoped projection slot identity
alias edits that would change ORDER BY output-name binding fail closed
projection-slot identities allow repeated source columns to be independently edited, added, removed, and reordered
repeated source columns remain editable, reorderable, and independently aliasable by projection slot
allowlisted aggregates over supported arguments

a typed SQL-tree operation appends a relation-free `(SELECT 1)` scalar subquery projection; the nested SELECT is parsed as ordinary editable nodes and the insertion preserves surrounding comments and clauses

bounded nested AND/OR/NOT trees of typed column-to-parameter and same-type column-to-column comparisons for supported comparison operators, single-value IN/NOT IN, two independently typed BETWEEN bounds, and LIKE/ILIKE parameter patterns
IS NULL and IS NOT NULL predicates
the SQL tree inspector can toggle NOT for parser-classified IN, BETWEEN, LIKE, ILIKE, SIMILAR TO, RLIKE, and IS predicates while preserving operands and comments
filter edits preserve surrounding clauses and reject unsafe source rewrites
the group-by toolbar selects simple Form columns
the SQL tree can append an existing typed expression from the same query scope and creates GROUP BY before HAVING/ORDER/LIMIT when absent
the authorized planner validates grouping semantics
the Sort toolbar edits simple columns; the SQL tree can append an existing same-query typed expression with ASC/DESC and optional NULLS FIRST/LAST
the SQL tree can create ORDER BY before LIMIT/OFFSET when absent
unqualified identifiers resolve explicit projection aliases before same-named Form columns; the editor retains the typed source binding
ASC or DESC
NULLS FIRST or NULLS LAST
the structure parser recognizes and edits non-negative Int64 literals as decimal strings without JavaScript number conversion
LIMIT and OFFSET can be set or removed independently; both absent removes the row-limit clause
LIMIT/OFFSET placement is inserted after ORDER BY when present
one self-join of the selected Form with explicit distinct aliases and a closed INNER/LEFT/RIGHT/FULL join-kind choice
ON must be left_alias.column = right_alias.column with matching supported scalar types; reversed equality operands fail closed
wildcard projection only; editing the join kind or ON expression preserves source trivia outside the edited tokens

WHERE supports bounded AND/OR/NOT trees of qualified parameter comparisons, single-value IN/NOT IN, two-bound BETWEEN, LIKE/ILIKE, and IS NULL/IS NOT NULL on qualified columns; adding a JOIN qualifies every supported predicate leaf; ORDER BY supports simple qualified columns with ASC/DESC and NULLS FIRST/LAST; unqualified references fail closed
filter and sort edits fail closed when comments in the query could be lost by AST serialization
adding a join qualifies existing supported single-relation WHERE/ORDER BY columns with the left alias and preserves surrounding clause text
unquoted aliases and columns resolve with SQL case folding; quoted identifiers remain exact
CROSS/NATURAL/USING, multiple joins, derived relations, reversed equality operands, and other ON expressions fail closed

an existing CTE name and only its one-part relation references resolved through the nearest lexical WITH scope can be renamed atomically with a typed Rust operation; nested same-name CTEs shadow outer declarations
a named name AS (SELECT 1) seed can be added to a query after checking only same-scope collisions; a CTE can be removed when no reference resolves to it and its edit span has no comments
CTE ordering, relation authoring within a CTE, and full body restructuring are not yet covered
every set-operation operand must be a SELECT query body
the SQL tree editor changes an existing UNION, INTERSECT, or EXCEPT operator and its default, ALL, or DISTINCT quantifier while preserving operand text and comments
a query node can append a typed SELECT 1 seed with the chosen operator and quantifier; the existing query is parenthesized to retain its grouping
either operand can be explicitly removed while preserving the other; removal fails closed when comments outside the retained operand would be dropped
a typed swap operation reorders the exact operand source ranges while preserving interstitial trivia; arbitrary operand replacement is not yet covered; BY NAME quantifiers remain read-only

identifier and literal leaves, binary operators, target types on CAST/TRY_CAST/SAFE_CAST/`::`/CONVERT/TRY_CONVERT, and Rust-rendered CAST wrappers on supported expression nodes use typed document operations and retain unedited source
cast target edits replace only the target type and preserve the original cast form; comment-bearing cast wrappers remain read-only; authorized planning validates conversion and result types
typed projection expressions can be wrapped in a registered COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, or MAX call with optional single-argument DISTINCT; argument types remain subject to authorized planner validation
the syntax-tree inspector can build a binary expression around a selected SELECT item or expression node from two typed expression nodes in the same query scope using the closed Rust operator enum
typed literal and identifier leaves can be created in place of an existing expression node; comment-bearing spans fail closed
any typed expression node can be replaced by an existing typed expression from the same query scope; comments in the replaced span and cross-query copies are rejected

the tree can wrap a selected expression in typed IN, NOT IN, BETWEEN, NOT BETWEEN, LIKE, NOT LIKE, IS NULL, or IS NOT NULL templates with editable literal seeds; comments in the selected operand fail closed
predicate negation is editable only on parser-classified IN, BETWEEN, LIKE, ILIKE, SIMILAR TO, RLIKE, and IS predicates; it preserves operands and comments
CASE branch count and ELSE presence can be edited with typed Rust operations; inserted branches use a typed TRUE or NULL seed and their expressions remain editable through the tree

A selected projection expression can be replaced with another typed expression node in the same document while preserving aliases and surrounding SQL; new projection items are not created through this operation
A typed expression from the SQL document can be appended to an existing SELECT list as a new projection item while preserving source outside the insertion point
Existing projection items can be removed without deleting comments in the removed span, and reordered when the SELECT list contains no comments; output outside the projection list remains unchanged

For registered aggregates, typed projection expressions can be wrapped in COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, or MAX with optional single-argument DISTINCT; existing arguments can be replaced by selecting another typed expression node; COUNT arguments can be appended or removed only when the Rust aggregate registry permits the resulting arity; other function calls and predicates are not constructed, and FILTER, OVER, ordered argument clauses, and subquery arguments remain read-only
the SQL tree can seed a scalar subquery as `(SELECT 1)` in a SELECT list; it does not create an arbitrary nested query or infer a relation for that nested scope
